messages:
Carol (support): Escalation from AcmeFinance — seeing sustained 429s and p95 spikes for their Dedicated pool since ~09:10 UTC. Customer says requests are being rate-limited even though they have reserved capacity. Attaching their minimal repro and sample headers they sent. :concerned:

Bob (sre): Can you paste the tenant id + request headers and a sample response body? 429 body usually includes throttling reason. :eyes:

Carol (support): Tenant: acme-fin-01
Example curl they used:
```bash
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'X-Redwood-Tenant: acme-fin-01' \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response: 429, body:
```json
{"error":"throttled","reason":"POOL_THROTTLED","pool":"dedicated:eu-west-1:pool-42"}
```
They say their Dedicated dashboard shows tokens well under quota.

oncall-bot: Alert: sustained 5xx/429 aggregate spike on dedicated-serving (eu-west-1) 09:08-09:16 UTC — routing fallbacks increased by +23%.

Dana (runtime): Repro locally with tenant header, got same 429s. Looking at router logs for that tenant ID now. Quick check: are we sure the tenant is pinned to pool-42?

Alice (control-plane): I pulled the routing decision trace for acme-fin-01 at 09:12:19 UTC — router matched policy tier=enterprise, but fallback ordered pools incorrectly: it chose shared:coldpool:eu-west-1 instead of dedicated:pool-42 when capacity was reported as transiently degraded. Full decision log: 
```
routing.trace: tenant=acme-fin-01 tier=enterprise matched_rule=pool_affinity
  candidate_pools=["shared:hot-eu","dedicated:eu-west-1:pool-42","shared:cold-eu"]
  health_states={"shared:hot-eu":"OK","dedicated:eu-west-1:pool-42":"DEGRADED","shared:cold-eu":"OK"}
  fallback_order from control-plane: ["shared:cold-eu","shared:hot-eu","dedicated:eu-west-1:pool-42"]
  chosen_pool=shared:cold-eu
```

Alice (control-plane): That fallback_order is wrong — dedicated pools should be preferred for pinned tenants. This looks like the new fallback-sorting change landed in yesterday's control-plane deploy. :facepalm:

Bob (sre): If dedicated pool was marked DEGRADED but still had capacity, choosing shared cold would impose stricter throttles. Need to verify health check false-positive. Any metric that shows pool-42 was actually healthy?

Dana (runtime): From the dedicated telemetry at 09:11: endpoint qps/slot for pool-42 was 42% utilized, latency 35ms. Health probe returned ERROR for one controller pod due to a transient /metrics scrape timeout. Controller flagged pool DEGRADED because of a single failed probe — our degradation threshold is 1 probe fail which is too aggressive.

Maya (acct-mgmt): Customer upset, billing unaffected but SLA complains. They're asking for root cause and timeline for fix. They want retries turned off for fallback to shared pools until we fix.

Carol (support): Repro steps we gave to them: 1) hit generate with X-Redwood-Tenant; 2) watch 429s; 3) check Control Plane > Routing > tenant affinity. They provided screenshots showing dedicated pool still in their console as GREEN.

Alice (control-plane): Two issues: (A) fallback sort priority got inverted in the rollout (PR #4821 changed comparator) — dedicated pools lost preference when a pool is DEGRADED; (B) health threshold too sensitive (1 probe). I have a quick patch: revert comparator and bump degrade threshold to 3 consecutive probe failures. Patch attached below.
```
// bad comparator (new)
return a.healthScore - b.healthScore || a.capacityScore - b.capacityScore;
// intended comparator (prefer dedicated affinity)
if (a.isDedicated !== b.isDedicated) return (b.isDedicated? 1 : -1);
return a.healthScore - b.healthScore;
```

Bob (sre): Can we hotfix control-plane config first to avoid more tenant re-routes? Otherwise more customers could get routed off their dedicated pools.

Dana (runtime): I can push a one-line rollback to control-plane routing-service and increase the health window in the same rollout. Will coordinate with infra. Estimated impact window ~30s for the rollout.

oncall-bot: Deploy queued: routing-service v2.14.7 -> v2.14.6 (rollback). CI checks green.

Carol (support): I told AcmeFinance we'll roll back the change and will follow up within 1 hour with a root cause and mitigation. They want a temporary mitigation we can apply to their tenant (pin to pool-42 bypassing fallback) — is that possible?

Alice (control-plane): Yes, I can add an explicit tenant override for acme-fin-01 to pin to dedicated:eu-west-1:pool-42 until the rollback is live. Doing that now.

Bob (sre): After rollback we should run a small chaos test: temporarily make controller probe fail for one pod and ensure we don't flip fallback order incorrectly. Also audit recent PRs touching comparator logic.

Maya (acct-mgmt): I'll send a short customer note: we identified a control-plane routing change that temporarily deprioritized dedicated pools under certain probe failures. We're rolling back and will follow with a postmortem.

Carol (support): FYI, customer also flagged that their logs showed "reason":"POOL_FALLBACK" on all 429s — that will be useful for the postmortem.

Dana (runtime): Rollback started 09:25 UTC. Monitoring will show routing-fallback percentage drop. I'll post back when 50%+ of traffic is back on dedicated pool-42.

Bob (sre): Thanks — once metrics settle, I'll open the incident P1 and collect timelines. We should include PR #4821 and the controller probe tuning in the postmortem. :thumbsup:

Carol (support): Customer updated: they see fewer 429s now, tokens accepted again. I'll keep thread open for postmortem notes. :relieved:
